Nothing was modified. The analysis covers `CircuitStateController<T>` in `src/Polly.Core`. The legacy `src/Polly` project has its own separate `CircuitStateController<TResult>`, which I excluded. I traced callers by reading and searching the code, not by running a call-graph tool. Bash was denied, so the test list comes from a name search, not from running the tests.

## Production methods that reach `EnsureNotDisposed`

**Depth 1: direct callers, all in `CircuitStateController<T>`**
- `CircuitStateController.CircuitState` (getter)
- `CircuitStateController.LastException` (getter)
- `CircuitStateController.LastHandledOutcome` (getter)
- `CircuitStateController.IsolateCircuitAsync`
- `CircuitStateController.CloseCircuitAsync`
- `CircuitStateController.OnActionPreExecuteAsync`
- `CircuitStateController.OnUnhandledOutcomeAsync`
- `CircuitStateController.OnHandledOutcomeAsync`

The private helpers (`CloseCircuit_NeedsLock`, `OpenCircuitFor_NeedsLock` and so on) are called by these methods, not the other way round. `CircuitStateController.Dispose` only sets the flag and does not call `EnsureNotDisposed`.

**Depth 2: callers of those methods in production code**
- `CircuitBreakerResilienceStrategy.ExecuteCore` calls `OnActionPreExecuteAsync`, `OnHandledOutcomeAsync` and `OnUnhandledOutcomeAsync`.
- The `CircuitBreakerResilienceStrategy` constructor (`CircuitBreakerResilienceStrategy..ctor`) reaches `CircuitState` through a lambda handed to `CircuitBreakerStateProvider.Initialize`. It reaches `IsolateCircuitAsync` and `CloseCircuitAsync` through `CircuitBreakerManualControl.Initialize`. If the manual control is created with `isIsolated: true`, `Initialize` calls `IsolateCircuitAsync` immediately.
- `CircuitBreakerStateProvider.CircuitState` (getter) invokes the stored `CircuitState` lambda.
- `CircuitBreakerManualControl.Initialize` calls `onIsolate` immediately when the control was created isolated.
- `CircuitBreakerManualControl.IsolateAsync` calls the registered `IsolateCircuitAsync` callbacks.
- `CircuitBreakerManualControl.CloseAsync` calls the registered `CloseCircuitAsync` callbacks.

**Depth 3 and beyond: everything that runs `ExecuteCore`**

`ExecuteCore` is reached through these internal components:
- `BridgeComponent.ExecuteCore`
- `BridgeComponent<T>.ExecuteCore` (`BridgeComponent.TResult.cs`)
- `CompositeComponent.ExecuteCore`
- `DelegatingComponent.ExecuteCore`
- `DelegatingComponent.ExecuteComponent`
- `DelegatingComponent.ExecuteComponentAot`
- `ExecutionTrackingComponent.ExecuteCore`
- `ExternalComponent.ExecuteCore`
- `ReloadableComponent.ExecuteCore`
- `ComponentWithDisposeCallbacks.ExecuteCore`
- `PipelineComponent.ExecuteCore` (the overload that takes a static callback)

The public entry points are all the `ResiliencePipeline` and `ResiliencePipeline<T>` execution methods:
- `ResiliencePipeline.Execute`
- `ResiliencePipeline.ExecuteAsync`
- `ResiliencePipeline.Execute<TResult>`
- `ResiliencePipeline.ExecuteAsync<TResult>`
- `ResiliencePipeline.ExecuteOutcomeAsync`
- `ResiliencePipeline<T>.Execute`
- `ResiliencePipeline<T>.ExecuteAsync`
- `ResiliencePipeline<T>.ExecuteOutcomeAsync`

These only reach the controller when the pipeline contains a circuit-breaker strategy, which `CircuitBreakerResiliencePipelineBuilderExtensions` builds, with `AddCircuitBreaker` as the public way to add one. The same applies to any pipeline that wraps one, for example one added with `AddPipeline`, or one resolved through `ResiliencePipelineRegistry` and `ResiliencePipelineProvider`.

I did not check whether other strategies in `src/Polly.Core` or `src/Polly.Extensions` run a pipeline from inside their own `ExecuteCore`. If any do, they would add more methods at this depth.

## Test files
Found by searching `test/` for `CircuitStateController`, `CircuitBreakerResilienceStrategy`, `CircuitBreakerManualControl`, `CircuitBreakerStateProvider` and `AddCircuitBreaker`.

Direct tests of the controller and its immediate callers:
- `test/Polly.Core.Tests/CircuitBreaker/Controller/CircuitStateControllerTests.cs`
- `test/Polly.Core.Tests/CircuitBreaker/CircuitBreakerResilienceStrategyTests.cs`
- `test/Polly.Core.Tests/CircuitBreaker/CircuitBreakerManualControlTests.cs`
- `test/Polly.Core.Tests/CircuitBreaker/CircuitBreakerStateProviderTests.cs`
- `test/Polly.Core.Tests/CircuitBreaker/CircuitBreakerResiliencePipelineBuilderTests.cs`

Tests that go through a built pipeline:
- `test/Polly.Core.Tests/Issues/IssuesTests.CircuitBreakerStateRegistry_1828.cs`
- `test/Polly.Core.Tests/Issues/IssuesTests.CircuitBreakerStateSharing_959.cs`
- `test/Polly.Extensions.Tests/Issues/IssuesTests.OnCircuitBreakWithServiceProvider_796.cs`
- `test/Polly.Extensions.Tests/Issues/IssuesTests.StrategiesPerEndpoint_1365.cs`
- `test/Polly.Testing.Tests/ResiliencePipelineExtensionsTests.cs`

Other test files may reach the controller through a pipeline that includes a circuit breaker without mentioning those names, so this list may be incomplete.
